about: The same dialect on a machine set to G-code system B (plan §8.1, AD-31): the machine, not the profile, decides which database and which power-on feed mode apply. Everything the codes mean changes with it — G92 is the speed clamp and not a threading cycle, G95 is feed per revolution, G78 cuts the thread, and G90/G91 are the distance codes this system has and system A has not, so `distance` starts unknown instead of absolute.

states.about: The power-on feed mode is G95 here, and it is assumed because the machine says so, not because the profile does (AD-19 rule 8). Unlike system A this database has distance codes, so nothing may be assumed about the distance mode until the program writes one.
`G21 G40 G90 G95` states all of it: absolute, millimetres, feed per revolution.

AD-19 rule 4 again, on the code that carries it in this system: the S of a G92 block is the clamp. In system A the same number is the single-pass threading cycle, which is the whole reason the system is a machine parameter.
G77 is the outer-diameter turning cycle of system B and an ordinary move as far as the feed goes: F0.3 is a feed per revolution.
G78 is the threading cycle of system B: its F is the 2 mm lead, and it stays in force over the pass blocks below.
A pass block written with the code again; still a thread.
G33 is a threading move in both systems.
